% image — a page whose only content is an image, and a caption.
%
% One concern: a page with no extractable prose must not be mistaken for a failure.
% "No text" is the honest answer here, and the whole point of the fixture is that
% the honest answer is distinguishable from a lost one — this is the case the md
% verb's empty-output warning must not fire on falsely, and the case the OCR router
% is supposed to select on coverage.
%
% The caption is what makes it a real test rather than a blank page: the page has
% exactly one line of text, so an extractor that returns nothing has lost something
% and an extractor that returns the body of some other page has invented something.
%
% image-bands.png is generated, not sourced: three flat colour bands at 64x48. Flat
% so extracted pixels are trivially checkable, and non-square so a transposed or
% rotated read shows up in the dimensions alone.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}

\includegraphics[width=4cm]{image-bands.png}

Figure 1: three colour bands.

\end{document}
